explain.say: When the plants died they fell into swampy water with little oxygen, so they did not fully rot. Layer on layer piled up into a soggy brown mass called peat.

faq.q: Why didn't the plants rot away?
faq.a: They fell into still swamp water with very little oxygen. The microbes that break down dead plants need oxygen, so the plant matter built up as peat instead of rotting.

faq.q: Why is coal called a fossil fuel?
faq.a: Coal is made from the remains of plants that lived hundreds of millions of years ago, so it is a fossil, and we burn it for energy. Sometimes you can even see fossil leaves in coal.

faq.q: How long does coal take to form?
faq.a: Millions of years. Peat builds up slowly, and turning it into hard coal takes millions of years of burial, heat and pressure, which is why coal is not renewable.

faq.q: Where does the energy in coal come from?
faq.a: Ancient plants captured energy from sunlight by photosynthesis and stored it in their bodies. That stored energy is released as heat when coal burns.

faq.q: Why is burning coal a problem?
faq.a: Burning coal releases carbon dioxide that was locked away for millions of years, which adds to climate change. It also gives off smoke and gases that pollute the air.
asks: Is coal bad for the environment?

facts: The Carboniferous Period, about 359 to 299 million years ago, is named after the large coal deposits from that time.
Peat turns into lignite, then bituminous coal, then anthracite as it is buried deeper and heated more.

quiz.say: Coal is mostly made from the remains of…
quiz.why: Coal formed from plant matter that built up in swamps and was buried and squeezed for millions of years.

wrong.1: Coal is plant remains; dinosaurs did not form coal.
wrong.2: Sea shells form limestone, not coal.
